metadata.case_name: LI WING KWAI v. CHAN HAU YU

injuries.description: soft tissue contusion injury to her left elbow/wrist, dorsal aspect of left hand as well as her right shoulder
source: (c) According to the Medical Report for insurance claim completed by Dr Lam (undated), Ms Li was injured on 26/2/11 after she had a brawl and was physically assaulted. The diagnosiswas soft tissue contusion injury to her left elbow/wrist, dorsal aspect of left hand as well as her right shoulder.

injuries.description: impingement syndrome and tendinosis or partial tear of the supraspinatus tendon of the right shoulder (precipitated symptomatic degeneration of the rotator cuff tendon)
source: (e) The cause of the persistent pain of her right shoulder was impingement syndrome and tendinosis or partial tear of the supraspinatus tendon.

(f) Since Ms Li has no past history of symptoms of impingement syndrome prior to the captioned incident and there was definite history of trauma to her right shoulder, the captioned accident should be regarded as the precipitating cause for the pain from the degenerated rotator cuff tendon in her right shoulder. On the other hand, it is impossible for me to say, if not for the accident, she could remain asymptomatic for how long from the date of the accident. It certainly can become symptomatic at any time due to stress to the shoulder from activities of daily living, housework or shopping.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of muscle or tendon of the rotator cuff of shoulder

injuries.description: contusion or sprain of the left thumb; diagnosis of ligament injury by orthopaedic colleagues
source: (a) According to the medical reports from the A&ED AHNH, he attended the A&ED at about 1 am on 27/2/11 for crushing injury to left thumb. Examination revealed tenderness, redness and bruise marks over left hand. X-ray of left thumb showed no fracture. He was discharged home. He attended the A&ED again at about 5 pm on 27/2/11 for left thumb contusion when being assaulted on 26/2/2011. Examination revealed swelling and tenderness of left thumb. The range of movement was decreased. He was referred to the DOT of AHNH.
(d) The diagnosis should be ‘contusion’ or ‘sprain’ of the left thumb. I consider the diagnosis of ligament injury made by the orthopaedic colleagues of AHNH to be appropriate.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of thumb, unspecified
